fields.title: Portfolio: which products a company needs simultaneously
fields.keyTakeaway: Products in a portfolio play different roles: some bring in money now, others grow on that money, and still others are bets on the future. The mistake is demanding the same metrics from all of them.
fields.checkQuestion: A new stream is given the same margin requirements as the core product. What will happen?
fields.blocks/0/text: Key question of the node: **which products does the company need?**
fields.blocks/1/items/0: **Cash cows** — high share in a mature market. They generate cash and require efficiency, not growth.
fields.blocks/1/items/1: **Stars** — high share in a growing market. They require investment so as not to lose position.
fields.blocks/1/items/2: **Question marks** — low share in a growing market. These are bets: some will become stars, some will close. Demanding profit from them means killing them.
fields.blocks/1/items/3: **Dogs** — low share in a mature market. Candidates for closure or for turning into a narrow profitable niche.
fields.blocks/2/text:
Book subscription — core, 92% of revenue, mature market. Goal: retention and cost of sales. Few experiments, low risk.

Audio versions — growing market, our share is small. Goal: not profit, but demand validation and cost per hour produced. Separate budget, separate metrics, right to shut down in a year.

Selling individual books without subscription — small share, mature market, support costs more than revenue. Candidate for closure; decision postponed for the second year in a row.

The main benefit of such a discussion is to stop comparing apples to oranges in a general meeting.
fields.blocks/2/title: Vetka, three products and three different conversations
fields.blocks/3/text: Bets require leadership attention even more than money. Three new directions usually mean that none of them gets enough of either.
fields.blocks/3/title: A company rarely handles more than one or two bets at once
fields.blocks/4/text: The matrix relies on market share and growth — numbers that are often estimates. It should be used as a language for discussing roles, not as a calculation tool.
